source: Public record: official government websites, Wikipedia office-holder pages and recent news reports. The playable leader and AI personality for each nation is its effective foreign-and-defence-policy leader (head of government in parliamentary systems, president in presidential systems, paramount/supreme leader in one-party states and Iran), not necessarily the ceremonial head of state. Office-holders were re-verified by web search on 2026-11-02; trait scores are the authors' editorial estimates derived from each effective leader's public statements and policy record

effectiveLeader.name: Donald Trump
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state, head of government and commander-in-chief and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Second-term record of tariff-driven economic nationalism, transactional treatment of NATO and other allies, and willingness to use force unilaterally (2025 Iran strikes, 2026 Venezuela operation) alongside deal-seeking with adversaries; midterm elections fall on 2026-11-03.

effectiveLeader.name: Xi Jinping
effectiveLeader.title: General Secretary of the CCP, Chairman of the Central Military Commission and President
effectiveLeader.basis: One-party state: the CCP General Secretary and CMC Chairman is the paramount leader; the Premier runs the State Council's economic administration.

headOfState.name: Xi Jinping
headOfState.title: President and General Secretary of the CCP

leaders.rationale: Long-horizon, risk-averse but assertive posture (Taiwan pressure, South China Sea, military modernisation) paired with a declared no-first-use doctrine and heavy emphasis on economic security; no competitive national elections are scheduled in the one-party system.

effectiveLeader.name: Vladimir Putin
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-presidential system in which the President directs foreign, defence and security policy and commands the armed forces; the Prime Minister manages the economy.

leaders.rationale: Full-scale invasion of Ukraine since 2022, repeated nuclear signalling and a 2024 lowering of the declared nuclear doctrine threshold, and a securitised worldview expressed in official speeches; the economy has been subordinated to the war effort.

effectiveLeader.name: Narendra Modi
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister and Cabinet direct foreign and defence policy; the President acts on ministerial advice.

leaders.rationale: Strategic autonomy and multi-alignment (Quad, BRICS, Russian energy purchases), assertive retaliation against Pakistan in 2019 and 2025, a declared no-first-use doctrine, and a governing agenda centred on growth and Hindu-nationalist identity.

effectiveLeader.name: Andy Burnham
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister directs foreign and defence policy; the monarch is ceremonial. Burnham succeeded Keir Starmer on 20 July 2026.

leaders.rationale: Burnham became PM in July 2026 after Keir Starmer's resignation, inheriting Labour's commitments to NATO, Ukraine support and the Trident deterrent while campaigning on a domestic, soft-left economic agenda; UK nuclear policy retains deliberate ambiguity but a very high bar.

effectiveLeader.name: Emmanuel Macron
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-presidential system: by constitutional practice the President leads foreign and defence policy (the domaine réservé) and controls the nuclear deterrent; the Prime Minister runs domestic government.

leaders.rationale: Macron's advocacy of European strategic autonomy, offers to extend France's nuclear umbrella to European partners, forward-leaning Ukraine proposals, and a fragile domestic position after repeated government collapses; the presidential election is due April 2027.

effectiveLeader.name: Friedrich Merz
effectiveLeader.title: Federal Chancellor
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: the Federal Chancellor sets policy guidelines including foreign and defence policy (and commands the armed forces in wartime); the Federal President is largely ceremonial.

headOfState.name: Frank-Walter Steinmeier
headOfState.title: Federal President
headOfState.party: Social Democratic Party (membership suspended in office)

leaders.rationale: Merz lifted the debt brake for defence, backs Ukraine strongly and has floated European nuclear-sharing talks with France and the UK, while Germany remains a non-nuclear state with a strong Atlanticist and export-economy orientation.

effectiveLeader.name: Sanae Takaichi
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy: the Prime Minister directs foreign and defence policy and commands the Self-Defense Forces; the Emperor is a symbol of the state with no governmental powers. Re-elected by the Diet on 18 February 2026 after the 8 February snap election.

leaders.rationale: Takaichi, re-elected after the February 2026 snap-election landslide, is a conservative who favours a faster defence build-up and a firm line on China and Taiwan while anchoring policy in the US alliance; Japan's three non-nuclear principles imply a very high nuclear bar.

effectiveLeader.name: Lee Jae-myung
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President directs foreign and defence policy and commands the armed forces; the Prime Minister is an appointed deputy.

leaders.rationale: Lee Jae-myung has pursued tension reduction with Pyongyang and pragmatic balancing between Washington and Beijing while keeping the US alliance and an economy-first agenda; South Korea is a non-nuclear NPT state under the US extended-deterrence umbrella.

effectiveLeader.name: Mojtaba Khamenei
effectiveLeader.title: Supreme Leader
effectiveLeader.basis: Islamic Republic: the Supreme Leader is head of state and commander-in-chief with final say on foreign, defence and nuclear policy; the elected President heads the executive under him. Mojtaba Khamenei was chosen by the Assembly of Experts on 8 March 2026 after Ali Khamenei was killed on 28 February 2026.

leaders.rationale: Mojtaba Khamenei, long described as his father's gatekeeper with close ties to the IRGC, took office in wartime in March 2026 and is widely reported to preside over an IRGC-dominated system in which elected President Pezeshkian has been sidelined; nuclear-threshold debates are now open in Tehran.

effectiveLeader.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister (caretaker)
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister and security cabinet direct foreign and defence policy; the President is ceremonial. Netanyahu remains caretaker PM after the 27 October 2026 election pending coalition formation (final results go to President Herzog on 4 November; the 26th Knesset is sworn in on 10 November).

leaders.rationale: Netanyahu has led multi-front wars in Gaza, Lebanon and against Iran (2025 and 2026) and resisted a Palestinian state; after the 27 October 2026 Knesset election left his bloc short of a majority he remains caretaker PM while coalition talks continue.

effectiveLeader.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Executive presidential system since 2018: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Cross-border operations in Syria and Iraq, S-400 purchase despite NATO membership, mediation between Russia and Ukraine, and a record of pressure on domestic opponents; allies have floated an early 2028 vote that would allow him to run again.

effectiveLeader.name: Shehbaz Sharif
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: constitutionally the Prime Minister and cabinet direct foreign and defence policy and the President acts on advice; in practice Field Marshal Asim Munir, army chief and since December 2025 Chief of Defence Forces, exerts major influence over security policy.

leaders.rationale: Shehbaz Sharif has prioritised IMF-backed economic stabilisation and close ties with China and Saudi Arabia while governing alongside a powerful military led by Field Marshal Asim Munir, under whom Pakistan fought the May 2025 clash with India; Pakistan's doctrine rejects no-first-use to offset conventional inferiority.

effectiveLeader.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President directs foreign and defence policy. Lula won the 25 October 2026 runoff and begins a new term on 5 January 2027 (his opponent has sought to annul the result).

leaders.rationale: Lula narrowly won the 25 October 2026 runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro; his record is non-aligned diplomacy, BRICS engagement, mediation offers on Ukraine and social spending, with Brazil a constitutional non-nuclear-weapon state.

effectiveLeader.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-presidential system under martial law: the President is commander-in-chief, chairs the National Security and Defence Council and leads foreign policy; the Prime Minister runs the cabinet.

leaders.rationale: Zelensky has led wartime resistance to Russia's invasion with deep-strike campaigns, close dependence on Western support and repeated diplomatic outreach on ceasefire terms; national elections remain suspended under martial law and Ukraine is a non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Lai Ching-te
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-presidential system: the President directs foreign, cross-Strait and defence policy and commands the armed forces; the Premier heads the Executive Yuan.

leaders.rationale: Lai's firm sovereignty rhetoric, increased defence spending and civil-defence drills in the face of PLA pressure, constrained by an opposition-controlled legislature that has stalled budgets; Taiwan renounced nuclear weapons programmes in the 1980s.

effectiveLeader.name: Kim Jong Un
effectiveLeader.title: President of the State Affairs Commission and General Secretary of the WPK
effectiveLeader.basis: One-party state: Kim Jong Un, as WPK General Secretary, President of the State Affairs Commission and supreme commander, is the paramount leader; the Premier handles economic administration.

headOfState.name: Kim Jong Un
headOfState.title: President of the State Affairs Commission and General Secretary of the WPK

leaders.rationale: A 2022 law enshrining pre-emptive nuclear use, continuous missile testing, troops and munitions supplied to Russia under the 2024 treaty, and the constitutional designation of South Korea as a hostile state; no competitive elections exist.

effectiveLeader.name: Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud
effectiveLeader.title: Crown Prince and Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Absolute monarchy in which the Crown Prince, also Prime Minister since 2022, runs day-to-day government including foreign and defence policy on behalf of the elderly King Salman.

leaders.rationale: The Crown Prince runs day-to-day government around Vision 2030 diversification, the 2023 China-brokered détente with Iran and hedging between Washington and Beijing, after the costly Yemen intervention; MBS has stated Saudi Arabia would seek a bomb if Iran acquired one; the absolute monarchy holds no national elections.

effectiveLeader.name: Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Federal monarchy: the President (ruler of Abu Dhabi) directs foreign and defence policy and commands the armed forces; the Prime Minister (ruler of Dubai) runs the federal cabinet.

leaders.rationale: Abraham Accords normalisation with Israel, active proxy involvement in Libya, Yemen and Sudan, deep investment diplomacy with both the US and China, and a civil nuclear programme under IAEA safeguards; the federation of hereditary rulers holds no competitive national elections.

effectiveLeader.name: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President directs foreign and defence policy and commands the armed forces; the Prime Minister manages the cabinet and economy.

leaders.rationale: Sisi's military-backed presidency is focused on regime security, mediation on Gaza, firm red lines on Rafah and Nile water (GERD), and reliance on Gulf, IMF and US financing; Egypt is a non-nuclear NPT state.

effectiveLeader.name: Donald Tusk
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers conduct foreign and defence policy; the President is commander-in-chief with a veto and a role in foreign representation, producing cohabitation friction.

leaders.rationale: Tusk, a former European Council president, has driven Europe's highest defence spending share of GDP, a hard line on Russia and Belarus and strong EU and NATO alignment, while facing cohabitation vetoes from President Nawrocki; Poland is a non-nuclear state seeking closer nuclear-sharing arrangements.

effectiveLeader.name: Giorgia Meloni
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister directs government policy including foreign and defence policy; the President is a largely ceremonial guarantor.

leaders.rationale: Meloni combines national-conservative domestic politics with reliable Atlanticism, support for Ukraine and a bridging role with the Trump administration, while cautious on fiscal commitments; Italy is a non-nuclear NATO host state.

effectiveLeader.name: Pedro Sánchez
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister directs foreign and defence policy; the King is ceremonial. A snap general election is set for 29 November 2026.

leaders.rationale: Sánchez has resisted NATO's 5% spending target, recognised Palestine and opposed Israel's Gaza campaign, and governs by minority coalition; after Congress rejected his housing decrees he called a snap general election for 29 November 2026.

effectiveLeader.name: Mark Carney
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister directs foreign and defence policy; the King and Governor General are ceremonial.

leaders.rationale: Former central banker who won a majority via 2026 by-elections, prioritising trade diversification and a US tariff deal, defence spending increases and sovereignty rhetoric in response to US pressure; Canada is a non-nuclear NATO member.

effectiveLeader.name: Anthony Albanese
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister and cabinet direct foreign and defence policy; the King and Governor-General are ceremonial.

leaders.rationale: Second-term Labor government continuing AUKUS submarines and US alliance while stabilising trade with China, and a 2026 budget centred on fuel security; Australia is a non-nuclear state under the US umbrella.

effectiveLeader.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Sovereignty-first but cooperative handling of US tariff and cartel pressure, judicial reform and continuity of social programmes with a congressional supermajority; Mexico is a Treaty of Tlatelolco non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Prabowo Subianto
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Former general pursuing free-and-active non-alignment (BRICS membership, balanced US-China ties), expanded military role in government and large state-led spending programmes; Indonesia is a non-nuclear NPT state.

effectiveLeader.name: Tô Lâm
effectiveLeader.title: General Secretary of the CPV and President
effectiveLeader.basis: One-party state: the CPV General Secretary is the paramount leader; Tô Lâm has held that post since August 2024 and was also elected State President on 7 April 2026.

headOfState.name: Tô Lâm
headOfState.title: President and General Secretary of the CPV

leaders.rationale: Tô Lâm consolidated party and state leadership in April 2026 after the 14th Party Congress, with former central-bank governor Lê Minh Hưng as PM, continuing bamboo diplomacy between China and the US and export-led growth; National Assembly elections are single-party and not competitive.

effectiveLeader.name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Expanded US basing access and assertive publicising of South China Sea confrontations with China, a bitter feud with the Duterte camp, and impeachment complaints dismissed by the House in February 2026; the Philippines is constitutionally nuclear-free.

effectiveLeader.name: Anutin Charnvirakul
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy: the Prime Minister directs government policy, though the monarchy and military retain significant informal influence. Anutin was re-elected PM by the new House on 19 March 2026.

leaders.rationale: Conservative coalition leader re-elected PM in March 2026 after Bhumjaithai topped the February election, following the 2025 border clashes with Cambodia; Thailand hedges between the US treaty alliance and China and is a non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Bola Tinubu
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state and government and commander-in-chief and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Market-oriented shock reforms (fuel subsidy removal, naira float), ECOWAS leadership during the Sahel coups, and an APC ticket secured for the January 2027 election amid security crises; Nigeria is a non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary-elected executive presidency: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Leads a Government of National Unity with the DA, pursues non-aligned BRICS diplomacy and brought the ICJ genocide case against Israel while weathering US aid and trade pressure; South Africa dismantled its nuclear arsenal in 1990.

effectiveLeader.name: Abiy Ahmed
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Federal parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister is chief executive and commander-in-chief; the President is ceremonial. Abiy was sworn in for a new five-year term on 5 October 2026.

leaders.rationale: Abiy was sworn in for a new term in October 2026 after the Prosperity Party's June landslide; his record includes the Tigray war, ongoing Amhara and Oromia insurgencies, the GERD completion and public insistence on Red Sea access that has strained ties with Eritrea and Somalia.

effectiveLeader.name: Javier Milei
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the President is head of state and government and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Radical libertarian austerity and deregulation strengthened by the October 2025 midterm win, close alignment with the US and Israel and withdrawal from multilateral forums; Argentina is a Tlatelolco non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Ulf Kristersson
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister (caretaker)
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister directs foreign and defence policy; the King is ceremonial. Kristersson continues as caretaker PM after the Riksdag rejected Magdalena Andersson on 15 October 2026; the Speaker has put Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist to a Riksdag vote on 3 November; if she fails, Kristersson is to be asked to try to form a government, and four failed votes force an extra election.

leaders.rationale: Kristersson took Sweden into NATO and raised defence spending, and now serves as caretaker PM after the centre-left bloc won a narrow majority on 13 September 2026 while the Riksdag continues government formation; Sweden is a non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Alexander Stubb
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.party: National Coalition Party (membership suspended in office)
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-presidential system: the constitution gives the President leadership of foreign policy (in cooperation with the government) and supreme command of the Defence Forces; the Prime Minister leads domestic and EU policy.

headOfState.name: Alexander Stubb
headOfState.title: President
headOfState.party: National Coalition Party (membership suspended in office)

leaders.rationale: Stubb, a former prime minister, leads Finland's foreign policy as a new NATO member with a closed Russian border, practising active values-based diplomacy on Ukraine and close engagement with Washington; Finland is a non-nuclear state with strong total-defence traditions.

effectiveLeader.name: Rob Jetten
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister and cabinet direct foreign and defence policy; the King is ceremonial. Jetten was sworn in on 23 February 2026.

leaders.rationale: Jetten leads a D66-CDA-VVD minority cabinet sworn in February 2026 after D66 narrowly beat the PVV, continuing strong Ukraine and NATO commitments and a pro-EU, centrist economic line; the Netherlands hosts US nuclear-sharing but has no weapons of its own.

effectiveLeader.name: Alexander Lukashenko
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Authoritarian presidential system: the President controls foreign, defence and security policy; the Prime Minister manages the economy.

leaders.rationale: Hosts Russian tactical nuclear weapons and Oreshnik missiles under the Union State, served as a staging ground for the 2022 invasion while avoiding direct troop commitment, and maintains tight domestic control; elections are held but not judged competitive by observers.

effectiveLeader.name: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev
effectiveLeader.title: President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system (new constitution in force from 1 July 2026): the President directs foreign and defence policy; the Prime Minister, reappointed with Kurultai consent on 31 August 2026, runs the cabinet.

leaders.rationale: Multi-vector foreign policy balancing Russia, China and the West, public refusal to recognise Russian annexations in Ukraine, and a 2026 constitutional overhaul creating a unicameral Kurultai and vice presidency; Kazakhstan gave up Soviet nuclear weapons in the 1990s.

effectiveLeader.name: Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
effectiveLeader.title: Emir
effectiveLeader.basis: Semi-absolute monarchy: the Emir holds executive authority and directs foreign and defence policy; the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister serves at his pleasure.

headOfGovernment.name: Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani
headOfGovernment.title: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs

leaders.rationale: Emir Tamim has positioned Qatar as a mediator in Gaza, Afghanistan and Iran-US channels, hosts the US Al Udeid air base and uses LNG wealth for investment diplomacy; Qatar is a non-nuclear state.

effectiveLeader.name: Ali al-Zaidi
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Federal parliamentary republic: the Prime Minister is chief executive and commander-in-chief; the President is largely ceremonial. Al-Zaidi's partial cabinet was approved on 14 May 2026.

leaders.rationale: Al-Zaidi, a businessman relatively new to politics, emerged as a compromise PM in April 2026 after US objections to Nouri al-Maliki, pledging a state monopoly on arms while balancing US pressure over Iran-aligned militias against the influence of Tehran after the 2026 Iran war.

effectiveLeader.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
effectiveLeader.title: President (transitional)
effectiveLeader.basis: Transitional presidential system under the March 2025 constitutional declaration: the President holds executive power with no prime minister and directs foreign and defence policy.

leaders.rationale: Former HTS leader governing under a March 2025 interim constitution with no prime minister, pursuing sanctions relief and reconstruction ties with Gulf states, Turkey and the West while managing sectarian violence and Israeli strikes; no national election date has been set in the transition.

effectiveLeader.name: Delcy Rodríguez
effectiveLeader.title: Acting President
effectiveLeader.basis: Presidential system: the Acting President exercises executive power, including foreign and defence policy, since Nicolás Maduro was seized by US forces on 3 January 2026.

leaders.rationale: Became acting president after US forces detained Nicolás Maduro in January 2026; she has engaged in US-backed transition talks and oil deals, promised elections under a renewed electoral authority without setting a date, and faces a returned opposition led by María Corina Machado.

effectiveLeader.name: Christopher Luxon
effectiveLeader.title: Prime Minister
effectiveLeader.basis: Parliamentary monarchy: the Prime Minister and cabinet direct foreign and defence policy; the King and Governor-General are ceremonial. A general election is due on 7 November 2026.

leaders.rationale: Business-oriented coalition leader facing a general election on 7 November 2026 after surviving an April caucus leadership vote; New Zealand maintains its nuclear-free legislation and a modest, Five Eyes-aligned defence posture.
